clue.text: Cold room's adapted in institution to form part of cell

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged letters sit inside the word for institution

parts.note: a home is a residential institution, such as a care home

indicators.note: adapted means changed in form, so the letters of room's are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of room's, with the S kept as fodder

explanation.surface: A biology lesson in which a chilly room in some institution is converted to illustrate the parts of a cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container; 'cell' points to biology, not a prison or phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A chromosome is a thread of DNA found in the nucleus, one component of a living cell.

clue.text: Hit with hand or end of arm

definitions.meaning: to strike someone lightly with an open hand
the band at the wrist end of a sleeve

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both a light slap and the turned-back band of a sleeve at the wrist.

clue.text: Bloody unusual?

definitions.meaning: meat cooked so lightly it is still red and bloody

explanation.definitionFit: Underdone steak is described as bloody, and something seldom seen is uncommon; one word covers both.

clue.text: Financial system that could bring company money

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer says to jumble the second word: those letters give CO, an abbreviation for company, followed by MONEY

explanation.surface: An economics textbook describing a system in which firms can make money.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer's first word is an anagram signal acting on its second, and those letters rearranged give CO (company) plus MONEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A national economy combining private enterprise with state ownership is the system economists name this way.

clue.text: Hence not a single Frenchwoman joined the French department

parts.note: hence means therefore, so
Mme, Madame, is a married Frenchwoman, as opposed to Mlle, a single one

explanation.surface: A married Frenchwoman joins a French administrative department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a single' tells you the Frenchwoman is a Madame, MME, not a Mademoiselle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme is one of the numbered administrative regions of northern France, named after its river.

clue.text: Economist's general style is something very hard to bear

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was a famous economist, so his possessive is Mill's
tone is the general character or style of something

explanation.surface: Reading an economist's writing in its general style is an ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy burden is called a millstone round one's neck, an image from the huge grinding stone.

clue.text: Part of wing that moves, producing alarm

definitions.meaning: the hinged section on an aircraft wing
a state of panic or agitation

explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft wing has a hinged movable section, and a panicky fuss is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Yob embracing eccentric genius in male clothing

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the yob word wraps around the rest

parts.note: a yob is a lout, a loutish youth

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of genius are jumbled

explanation.surface: A thug hugs an oddball genius who is dressed in men's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' signals the anagram and 'embracing' the container. A yob is British slang for a rowdy young man.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge suit is a man's matching jacket and trousers for everyday formal wear.

clue.text: Inclination to show compassion about unfortunate person

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the compassion word goes round the jumbled letters

parts.note: pity means compassion

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of person are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tendency to feel compassion for someone down on their luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunate' signals the anagram and 'about' the container; 'to show' just links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A propensity is a natural tendency or leaning towards some behaviour.

clue.text: Supporting wife no more with plenty, perhaps

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
an ex is a former wife
ample means plentiful, enough

explanation.surface: A divorced man still supporting his ex with plenty of money, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps and the answer both introduce an illustration or possibility, as in 'say'.

clue.text: French author's expression of affection and love

definitions.note: here the 's stands for 'is', so the clue reads 'French author is ...'

parts.note: a hug is a physical expression of affection
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A French novelist expresses affection and love.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay rather than making the author possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo was the French novelist who wrote Les Misérables.

clue.text: Snack food making King Edward, perhaps, extremely thin

definitions.text: Snack food making King Edward, perhaps, extremely thin

parts.words: Snack food making King Edward, perhaps, extremely thin
parts.note: King Edward is a variety of potato, so the clue describes a snack made by slicing one very thinly

explanation.definitionFit: Packet snacks are made from potatoes such as the King Edward variety cut into wafer-thin slices and fried.

clue.text: Plant ground with seed at random

indicators.note: at random means in no particular order, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener sows seed haphazardly in the ground to grow a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'random' scrambles GROUND, SEED and AT together; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Adder's tongue is a small fern named for its spike, which resembles a snake's tongue.

clue.text: Fight Mark and others for material worth recycling

parts.note: a scrap is a brawl or fight
et al, Latin et alii, means and others

explanation.surface: Mark and his friends fight over stuff worth recycling.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded iron and steel is collected and melted down for reuse.

clue.text: Like staff serving drink in cans

definitions.meaning: bar staff work at the back of the counter
in prison, 'can' being US slang for jail

explanation.definitionFit: Barmen work on the far side of the counter, and prisoners are locked in cells; one phrase fits both.

clue.text: Goal in soccer involved raising of players' performance level

indicators.note: in places the goal word inside the jumbled letters
involved means complicated or tangled, so the letters of soccer are rearranged

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: Scoring a goal in a football match lifts the players' level of performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion. The players are musicians, not footballers.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is a gradual increase in loudness in music, the players raising their volume.

clue.text: Definite article?

parts.note: not 'the' of grammar but a product sold under a well-known, clearly identified label

explanation.definitionFit: A product from a recognised manufacturer is an item clearly identified by its label.

clue.text: Fools and what they were soon parted from in Rome?

definitions.text: what they were soon parted from in Rome?
definitions.meaning: a fool and his money are soon parted; the as was a Roman coin

explanation.definitionFit: Stupid people are donkeys, and Roman bronze coins also bear the same plural name.

clue.text: Like many flying from India via Nepal

indicators.note: from tells us to take the letters out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Many travellers fly from India via Nepal.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'India', all of 'via' and the start of 'Nepal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Avian means relating to birds, which describes most creatures that fly.

clue.text: One can recall submarine captain heading north in poor visibility

indicators.note: in places the captain and compass point inside the weather word

parts.note: mist is a cause of poor visibility

indicators.note: heading here means going in front of, so the captain comes before the compass point

parts.note: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel

explanation.surface: A submarine captain sets course north through the mist.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Nemo, of Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea, is a stock crossword submariner.
explanation.definitionFit: A mnemonist is a person with trained powers of memory, able to recall long lists.

clue.text: Emma, distressed with bad, love, needing change

definitions.text: Emma, distressed with bad, love, needing change

indicators.note: distressed means upset or troubled, so the letters of Emma and bad are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
to vary is to change

explanation.surface: A heroine upset by a bad love affair craves a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' signals the anagram of the first two pieces. The whole clue also sums up Flaubert's heroine Emma, unhappy in love and longing for change.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaubert's novel heroine, Emma, is trapped in a dull marriage and seeks escape in disastrous affairs.

clue.text: In pursuit of sex, American soldier left watch

indicators.note: in pursuit of means following behind, so the soldier and the letter for left come after

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, which is VI in Roman numerals
GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier chasing sex leaves his post on watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex' is the Latin word for six, giving VI, which the soldier and L follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a period of staying awake to keep watch.

clue.text: Entertain a lot of the audience?

indicators.note: of the audience means as heard by listeners, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: Is it possible to entertain most of the people watching?
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' looks like 'many', but means one's lot, fate, which is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To fête someone is to honour and entertain them lavishly.

clue.text: Equipment cut by new contract

indicators.note: cut by means divided by something placed in the middle

parts.note: kit is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: A set of gear is undercut by a fresh contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' is a verb: to draw together, as brows do.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit one's brows is to draw them together, to contract them in a frown.

clue.text: Defrost fruit after short time

indicators.note: after places the fruit following the short time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a haw is the red fruit of the hawthorn

explanation.surface: Defrost the fruit after a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: To thaw frozen food is to let it warm up until the ice melts.

clue.text: Fruit-tree observed, over time, appearing beside another

indicators.note: appearing beside puts the two pieces next to each other

parts.note: another fruit-tree, here a mango

indicators.note: over means covering, so the seen word goes over the time letter

parts.note: observed means seen

explanation.surface: A fruit-tree spotted, after a while, growing beside a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' asks for a second fruit-tree; 'over' means the observed word covers the time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The mangosteen is a tropical tree bearing a sweet purple fruit.

clue.text: Was inferior to other team — get this to beat it!

definitions.meaning: 'get' plus this word makes a phrase meaning go away, beat it

explanation.definitionFit: A beaten team was defeated, and telling someone to go away uses the same word after 'get'.

clue.text: Article in French a US teacher brought round for youth

indicators.note: brought round means placed around, so the teacher word surrounds the article

parts.note: a docent is a teacher or lecturer in American universities
les is the French plural definite article

explanation.surface: A French article is brought round by an American teacher for a young person.
explanation.walkthrough: Docent is American usage for a college teacher; 'brought round' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a youth, growing from child to adult.
